claims.text: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi can be prepared as a homogeneous, single-phase solid solution.
The equimolar CoCrFeNiTi solid solution has relatively low hardness and strength.
Random lattice distortions in this alloy enable unusually high dislocation mobility.
High dislocation mobility promotes extensive dynamic recovery during deformation.
Reduced dislocation accumulation lowers work hardening, hardness, and strength.
Thermal activation in the distorted equimolar solid-solution lattice facilitates rapid dislocation motion and dynamic recovery.
Increasing strain rate or lowering temperature suppresses dynamic recovery.
At room temperature and low strain rate, dislocations will move rapidly and form few pile-ups.
At high strain rate or low temperature, dislocation accumulation and entanglement will increase relative to the room-temperature, low-strain-rate baseline.
The increased dislocation accumulation and entanglement under recovery-suppressing conditions will produce higher yield strength and hardness.
The proposed mechanism applies only to equimolar CoCrFeNiTi retained in a single-phase solid-solution state without deformation-induced phase separation or precipitation.
Dislocation density and dynamic-recovery signatures can be compared across strain-rate and temperature conditions using in situ TEM and post-mortem measurements.
